question: Can an EUR/USD macro-surprise continuation family be tested now without hindsight or an unsourced consensus archive?
requirements: actual first-release value and exact UTC release timestamp
consensus forecast frozen before the release
previous value as known before the release and explicit revisions
point-in-time retrieval or immutable historical snapshot
license permitting internal research and storage of derived evidence
EUR/USD bid/ask observations around the event window

source_audit.capability: Historical vintages identify what official observations were known during a past real-time period.
source_audit.missing_for_surprise: Does not supply the market consensus forecast needed to calculate actual-minus-expected surprise.

source_audit.capability: Documents exact UTC event time, actual, previous, revised, survey consensus and point-in-time calendar retrieval.
source_audit.boundary: Requires API credentials and a license/subscription appropriate to PIT history and derived research; none is configured locally.

operational_rule: Do not substitute revised actuals, vendor forecasts, current calendar pages or model-generated forecasts for the consensus that existed immediately before each release.
cheap_next_step: Request or purchase only a small PIT pilot covering a few high-impact US and euro-area releases, then measure event frequency and gross post-release movement before any broad subscription or SQ generation.
